narration.text: A federal grant drawn down against what was spent, and the quarter's SF-425 filed. This is a chore for the finance manager of a twenty-person adult literacy nonprofit in Spokane, Washington, nine days after its federal award's quarter closed. Athena works it across 4 portals: Grantflow Payments, Docshelf, Ledgerline accounting and Payroll Harbor. On the bench, she found 6 of 6 eligible items, worth 31,492 dollars and 60 cents of the 31,492 dollars and 60 cents there was to find. All 6 were filed at the exact amount the rules allow. She made no false claim. The world held 9 traps, and she walked past 9. Among them: A curriculum license bought before the award began, recoded to it a year later. Tablets already drawn in July. She took 3 minutes. By hand, the same chore takes 8 hours, so she was about 141 times faster. The verdict: exceeds. She beat the bar this playbook set itself. The bar was 75 percent of the money, no false claim and inside 60 minutes. Every card she filed waited for a person's signature, and nothing was sent.
